correctness.rationale: For the fixed oriented tetrahedral faces, write B for the first three columns. The remaining column is -B1; B has full column rank, so (B D^{1/2})^+ B=D^{-1/2}. Thus the preconditioned operator is exactly D^{-1/2} M D^{-1/2} for M=diag(a,1,1/a)+11^T. The inherited choice gives I+vv^T with squared length 1/a+1+a, hence condition number 2+a+1/a. With D=diag(M), an independent symbolic determinant of lambda I-D^{-1}M gives (lambda-1)(lambda^2-2lambda+1/2)-a lambda/(1+a)^2. The three simple positive roots at a=0 justify the O(a) condition-number estimate about 3+2 sqrt(2). For any D, the leading principal block has invariant correlation c=[2(1+a)]^{-1/2}; its normalized determinant det/(trace)^2 is at most (1-c^2)/4, so by interlacing the full condition number is at least (1+c)/(1-c). This bound is uniform over all positive D and squeezes the infimum to the claimed order. The reciprocal sharp ratio follows directly. There is no claim of a finite-a optimum, variable face selection, or stability in finite precision.

value.rationale: A fixed retained subcomplex is a natural constraint in Hodge preconditioning. This sharp example distinguishes improving conditioning from approximating the operator in norm, and quantifies when inherited weights lose by order 1/a despite a simple bounded correction. The universal lower bound makes it an exact benchmark for positive reweighting, not merely a choice of an improved heuristic; no claim about larger meshes, running time or better face selection is needed.
